title: Loop language: two checks
description: Sum-free sets without two consecutive numbers. One check solver looks for sums, a second one for neighbours.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Rules every solver needs. The constant n is set in the Loop tab.
num(1..n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Solver A proposes candidates: here, any set of numbers.
{ pick(X) : num(X) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The atoms solver A and solver C share. glue(T) makes T an interface atom:
% its value in a candidate is fixed when the check runs.
glue(pick(X)) :- num(X).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: every glue(T) makes T an interface atom.

fragments.name: sums
fragments.text:
% Solver C looks for a counterexample: a sum X + Y = Z inside the candidate.
1 { sum(X,Y) : num(X), num(Y), X <= Y, X + Y <= n } 1.
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(Y).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X+Y).
#show sum/2.

% relevant(T): the interface atoms the counterexample depends on.
% The refinement says: at least one of them must change.
relevant(pick(X)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
relevant(pick(X+Y)) :- sum(X,Y).
fragments.description: The first check: a sum inside the set.

fragments.name: neighbours
fragments.text:
% The second check: two consecutive numbers in the set.
1 { next(X) : num(X), num(X+1) } 1.
:- next(X), not pick(X).
:- next(X), not pick(X+1).
relevant(pick(X)) :- next(X).
relevant(pick(X+1)) :- next(X).
fragments.description: The second check: two consecutive numbers.

loop.text:
solver A  = shared + abstraction
solver C1 = shared + sums
solver C2 = shared + neighbours
link   G1 = A -> C1 via shared + glue
link   G2 = A -> C2 via shared + glue

# Two checks: C2 runs only when C1 finds nothing. Whichever finds a
# counterexample, its own link turns it into the refinement.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C1.solve(assume G1(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G1.clause(M, X)
        else:
            Y = C2.solve(assume G2(M))
            if Y: reject M with G2.clause(M, Y)
